trust_decision.summary: Schema-supplied `x-python-import` (dict module/name) and `customTypePath` strings are trusted as Python import paths: JsonSchemaParser joins them into a dotted path and hands it to `Import.from_full_path`, whose module part is emitted verbatim as `from <module> import <name>`, so a value containing a newline breaks out of the generated import line (code injection into the generated file). Each consumer must validate before the primitive is called.

landing_point.why: Grep for the advisory's `x-python-import` extension lands here: the schema extras dict is unpacked into module/name and f-stringed straight into `Import.from_full_path` with no validation, on every `$ref` into a `$defs` entry. The second half of the summary (`customTypePath`) sits at 4096 and 4338, so a reader who fixes only these three places believes the report is closed.

fix_sites.entry_point: datamodel-codegen CLI (src/datamodel_code_generator/__main__.py:1196) or datamodel_code_generator.generate(); reached by any $ref to a $defs entry carrying x-python-import
same public entry points, reached only when an x-python-type annotation names a type that is also a $defs entry with x-python-import (two extensions combined)
same public entry points, property/sub-schema carrying customTypePath (also reachable from OpenAPI input, e.g. tests/data/openapi/shadowed_imports_base_and_fields.yaml:20)
same public entry points, root/enum-level schema carrying customTypePath (path is marked `# pragma: no cover` at the pinned commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fix is applied where the schema is read, so `DataTypeManager.get_data_type_from_full_path` can be argued to be a trusted internal primitive with only two in-tree callers, both now guarded — not part of the attack surface.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Arbitrary third-party dotted import paths are the feature itself: `customTypePath: mymodule.node.Node` (tests/data/openapi/shadowed_imports_base_and_fields.yaml:20), dotted `x-python-type` names resolved by `extract_qualified_names`, and `--external-ref-mapping` packages must all keep generating imports. An over-broad fix (denylisting os/sys, requiring stdlib, rejecting more than two parts, or validating inside `Import.from_full_path` itself) breaks these legitimate routes.

O6_input_shapes: x-python-import as a dict {module, name} on a $defs entry reached by $ref (get_ref_data_type)
the same dict reached only through an x-python-type annotation that names the $defs entry (_resolve_type_import_from_defs)
x-python-import dict with only one of module/name (fix makes this a hard error: 'x-python-import requires both module and name')
x-python-import that is not a dict at all, e.g. a bare string (still silently ignored, falls back to a $ref reference)
customTypePath as a root-level schema string (parse_root_type)
payload placed in `name` inside the dict vs embedded in the whole `customTypePath` string, with newline and quote characters

O8_uncovered_routes.route: x-python-type annotation: dotted prefix and qualified names go straight to Import.from_full_path (2086, 2092) with no dotted-identifier check; the only guard is the AST annotation check in types.py:353-392, a different mechanism
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: x-python-type is already constrained to a valid Python type annotation (is_python_type_annotation), so a newline or quote can never reach the import, and the project already has its own rejection test for that extension (tests/main/jsonschema/test_main_jsonschema.py:10898) — it is a neighbouring feature, not the reported one.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different extension and call chain (x-python-type vs x-python-import)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: apply the same dotted-path validator to the x-python-type-derived prefix and qualified names before Import.from_full_path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file and same sink, and the project already ships one 'reject unsafe <extension>' test per extension (default_factory, x-python-type, validators config), so a maintainer hardening import construction would naturally extend the validator to x-python-type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate inside DataTypeManager.get_data_type_from_full_path so the primitive cannot be misused by a new caller
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix chose call-site validation; a defensive maintainer could instead (or additionally) guard the primitive that every customTypePath path funnels through, which is exactly the kind of second site a task can pin.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: external-ref mapping builds f'{python_package}.{class_name}' directly into Import.from_full_path, with a comment saying 'same pattern as x-python-import'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Identical construction pattern in the same method cluster; a maintainer fixing import-path injection would review it, even though the package half comes from CLI config rather than the schema.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: validate the module/name produced by the --input-model $defs builder (__module__/__name__ of loaded classes) before injecting x-python-import
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This builder is the in-tree producer of x-python-import dicts; validating at production instead of consumption is the obvious alternative fix, and a sibling task could pin it.

O9_family: code injection into generated source, via schema-controlled import paths (CWE-94/CWE-95)

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend, uv (uv.lock present), tox + pytest
O10_build.project_tests: tests/main/jsonschema/test_main_jsonschema.py drives the CLI through run_main_and_assert (tests/main/conftest.py:486); tests/parser/test_jsonschema.py:1469 unit-tests _resolve_type_import_from_defs; tox.ini [testenv] runs the whole tests/ tree under pytest. The affected area uses only local schema fixtures, so it is offline-testable.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject newlines/quotes on the two strings the report shows (customTypePath in parse_item and the x-python-import $ref->$defs path) and stop; the real trap is that any Error raised inside _resolve_type_import_from_defs (jsonschema.py:2054-2063) is swallowed by its bare `except Exception` and degrades to 'no import', so validation added there silently passes unless the fix also re-raises Error.

out_of_scope_notes: tests/main/jsonschema/test_main_jsonschema.py already carries earlier 'reject unsafe' guards and tests for default_factory (3319), x-python-type (10898) and validators config (11412) — likely the sibling advisories; noted only, not pursued.
